newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe stocks end mixed amid profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe stocks end mixed amid profit-taking.

text.p: Zimbabwean stocks traded mixed on profit-taking on Thursday but brokers said they expected the market to resume its upward march as long as the rains continued.

The key 57-share industrial index -- which has been scaling new peaks in the past week -- dropped 51.21 points to close at 8,128.65, dragged down largely by blue-chip conglomerate Delta's 50-cent loss to 3,350.
"There was some profit-taking but the blue chips in general are still strong. As long as it continues to rain the market will continue to hold its own," one broker said.

Also among the losers, timber producer Border shed 50 cents to 1,250, tyre manufacturer Dunlop and construction group Mash each dropped 30 cents to 150 and 200 respectively, pharmaceutical firm Caps traded 25 cents off at 425 while pork processor Colcom at 360 and wine producer Afdis at 425 both lost 15 cents.

Gains were recorded in steel windows manufacturer Radar (30 cents up to 250), furniture and clothing retailer Tedco (25 cents up to 750) and sugar refinery ZSR (10 cents up to 1,390) while clothing retailer Edgars, hotel chain Zimsun, bankers FMB and textiler Spinweave traded unchanged in reasonable turnover.
Minings were quiet in thin trading with gold producer Rio Tinto rising 200 cents to 3,500 and Wankie Colliery adding five cents to 445. Falcon -- a gold mining investor -- slid 500 cents to 1,200.
The seven-counter mining index rose 24.08 points to 1,200.29.
